subject: Model fit & safety evals — next steps and prompt sets
messages:
From: Sara Jones <sara.jones@healthscope.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Tran <mike.tran@healthscope.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks + follow-up from today's discovery call

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call earlier — Mike and I appreciated the run-through of Redwood's serving options. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks: 

- Primary use case: internal triage assistant for clinician intake (short summaries, suggested next steps). Sensitive content (PHI) is possible in some prompts.
- Volume: ~200k requests/month, bursty during business hours.
- Success criteria: high refusal/deflection accuracy for disallowed requests, medically-safe answers (no fabricated diagnoses), and throughput <200ms 95th p50 for short summaries.

As next steps, could you share:
1) Recommended model(s) and quantization profiles to evaluate for this workload.
2) Example prompt sets we can run internally.
3) Any existing safety/refusal evals you can share for medical/sensitive domains.

We can start a short evaluation run next week if you can provide the prompt set and benchmark template. Attaching the notes I took during the call (see: call-notes.docx) — I can send the dataset excerpt once procurement signs off.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Jones
Director, Clinical Automation
HealthScope

Hi Sara — great to meet you both today, and thanks for the clear requirements. Quick post-call recap + next steps from our side: 

Recap
- Primary ask: safe, non-hallucinating clinical summaries and triage suggestions.
- Constraints: PHI may appear in input; we should treat PHI as sensitive and prefer refusal/redaction when unsure.

Immediate next steps
- Rafael (SE) will send recommended model variants and a starter prompt set (attached: proposed-prompt-sets.md).
- I'll share our benchmark template (CSV) and a Drive folder where you can drop an excerpt.
- Rishi (security) will follow up with safety evaluation artifacts and recommended guardrail prompts.

Attachments: proposed-prompt-sets.md (starter prompts + evaluation instructions)

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@healthscope.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Tran <mike.tran@healthscope.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Model recommendations + eval benchmark template

Hi Sara / team,

Following up with concrete recommendations for the eval run. I've attached a CSV benchmark template (healthscope-eval-benchmarks.csv) that maps input prompts -> expected behavior (accept/deflect/refuse + allowed output examples). Please use that as the canonical format so we can compare model outputs across runs.

Recommended model variants to evaluate (start with the first two rows):
- Redwood-Instruct-13B-quant (q4_0): cost-effective baseline with good instruction following; we expect strong summary quality for non-sensitive prompts.
- Redwood-70B-llama-fine-tuned (q5_1): higher quality/recall for complex summaries; more expensive but better at avoiding omissions.

Quick notes on quantization: q4_0 yields strong latency/cost tradeoffs for p50/p95 throughput. q5_1 is higher quality but consider 4-bit quant for cost saving if throughput becomes a bottleneck.

Safety and refusal behavior
- We've included guardrail prompt templates in the attached prompt set. Two patterns we suggest: explicit refusal style and safe-handoff to human. Example refusal prompt: 

  "I can’t help with personal medical diagnoses or provide instructions that could cause harm. For clinical questions, please contact your healthcare professional."

- For PHI inputs we recommend server-side redaction + a final check: if the model attempts to invent a diagnosis or provide definitive instructions, treat the response as a fail in the benchmark.

Attached: healthscope-eval-benchmarks.csv, proposed-prompt-sets.md

If you'd like, we can provision a sandbox tenant with the two model variants for 7 days so you can run the exact benchmark and return results. Let me know the test-owner and expected start date and I'll provision.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
From: security@healthscope.com <security@healthscope.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model recommendations + eval benchmark template

Thanks Rafael — a couple of security/compliance questions before we spin up a sandbox: 

1) Handling PHI: can the model be configured to never return verbatim PHI from training data? We need guarantees around data retention and that the model won't echo patient identifiers.
2) Auditability: do you have per-request logs we can export for our SOC2 auditors? Retention policy?
3) Safety evals: can you share prior refusal evaluation results against medical prompts or the methodology you use to score refusal/deflection?

If you can send a short one-pager or artifacts we can share with our InfoSec team, that will speed procurement.

Thanks,
HealthScope Security
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: security@healthscope.com, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model recommendations + eval benchmark template

Hi — looping in from Redwood's security team to address these questions and share initial artifacts. Summary below and attached a short PDF with eval results for medical refusal cases (safety-eval-results.pdf).

1) PHI handling:
- We recommend server-side redaction of identifiers before sending to the model. Additionally, our serving runtime supports response filters to block outputs that match PHI patterns (SSNs, MRNs, phone numbers). While we cannot retroactively remove information from a pre-trained model's weights, our benchmark and evals focus on the model's tendency to hallucinate or echo identifiers; we score those as fails.

2) Auditability / logs:
- Per-request metadata (timestamp, model, route id, token counts, response hash) can be exported to your S3 or a secure syslog. Retention defaults to 90 days; enterprise plans can extend to 1–3 years.

3) Safety evaluation methodology:
- We run a suite of 1k+ prompts across sensitive domains (medical, legal, finance) and label expected behavior: ACCEPT / REDACT / REFUSE. The attached PDF includes refusal precision/recall at different confidence thresholds for the models we recommended. 

Sample refusal wording we recommend embedding in the system prompt: 

  "I’m not able to provide medical diagnoses or treatment plans. If you need medical advice, please contact a qualified healthcare professional. I can help summarize medical records or escalate to a human clinician."

Next steps we can take for HealthScope:
- Provision a limited sandbox with request-level audit logs and response-filtering enabled.
- Run the 7-day benchmark with the CSV you provide; we will return a results CSV and a short summary PDF.

I'll share the PDF and a short one-pager for procurement in a follow-up email.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Security & Privacy, Redwood Inference
